newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: BNP says Indian guerrillas may target Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: BNP says Indian guerrillas may target Bangladesh.

text.p: The secretery-general of the opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) warned guerrillas in northeast India might turn their guns on Bangladesh because of Dhaka's "provocative activities."

"India wants to use Bangladesh as a springboard to crush the guerrillas...and the (Bangladeshi) government has become serious about cooperating with Indian forces," Abdul Mannan Bhuiya was quoted on Friday by the Bangladesh Observer newspaper as saying.
"Resorting to such provocative activities is making Bangladesh the target of guerrillas in northeast India," he told a meeting in Narsingdi, 80 km (50 miles) from Dhaka, on Thursday.

Bhuiyan criticised the government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina for cooperating with India, which he said was harbouring tribal rebels waging a separatist war in Bangladesh's Chittagong Hill Tracts.
He also blasted the government for trying to give India a land transit and access to sea ports for movement of troops and military equipment.
Government officials earlier said Dhaka had no such plans but they were not available on Friday for comments.
The allegations by Bhuiyan followed remarks by BNP chief Begum Khaleda Zia, former prime minister, that India was trying to use Bangladesh "to crush those fighting for independence."
"(Our) people will never allow Bangladesh to be used to suppress the struggle for liberation there," Dhaka's influential Bhorer Kagoj newspaper quoted Khaleda on Monday as saying.
Bangladesh and India recently agreed to work together to quell insurgency along their borders.
India has long faced a bloody insurgency in its seven northeastern states bordering Bangladesh, Burma and China.
Bangladesh has been fighting tribal Shanti Bahini guerrillas in the Hill Tracts for 23 years in a dispute that has claimed 8,500 lives.
